hypotheses.title: SingleProviderHelper._calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee unchecked overflow — no guard unlike FixedHelper counterpart
hypotheses.mechanism: SingleProviderHelper._calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee (line 170-171) performs `unchecked { amountInAfterFees = reserveAmountIn + lpFeeAmount; }` without any overflow guard. The identical function in FixedHelper (lines 1067-1072) includes an explicit check: `if (amountInAfterFees < lpFeeAmount) { revert FixedPool__Overflow(); }`. When sqrtPriceX96 is near MIN_SQRT_RATIO (~2^32) and amountOut is ~2^127 (max uint128 reserve), calculateFixedOutput returns reserveAmountIn ~2^255. With poolFeeBPS >= 5001, lpFeeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(2^255, 5001, 4999) > 2^255, and their sum overflows uint256. The wrapped amountInAfterFees becomes near-zero, making the swap appear to cost almost nothing for full reserves. The AMM's _validateProtocolFees at lines 1660-1663 catches this downstream because totalFees > wrapped amountIn always holds when overflow occurs, but SingleProviderHelper itself silently produces corrupted values — a defense-in-depth gap exploitable if AMM validation is ever relaxed or bypassed.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Confirmed SingleProviderHelper line 170-171 has unchecked addition with no overflow guard. FixedHelper lines 1067-1072 has explicit guard. When MIN_SQRT_RATIO price causes calculateFixedOutput to produce ~2^255 reserveAmountIn, fee sum overflows.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: Attacker: (1) SingleProvider pool with hook returning sqrtPriceX96 near MIN_SQRT_RATIO (4295128739). (2) Pool has ~2^127 output token reserves, poolFeeBPS = 5001. (3) Calls swapByOutput for full reserves. (4) calculateFixedOutput returns reserveAmountIn ~2^255. (5) lpFeeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(2^255, 5001, 4999) ~= 2^255.0003. (6) unchecked sum overflows uint256, wrapping to near-zero. (7) AMM's _validateProtocolFees catches it but pool type returns corrupted state — if validation bypassed, attacker drains reserves for 0 cost.
hypotheses.victim: AMM protocol and pool token holders — attacker could drain reserve tokens paying near-zero input if downstream validation is bypassed.

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper._increaseHeight post-loop spurious _crossHeight corrupts nextHeightAbove pointer and fee growth outside values
hypotheses.mechanism: After the main liquidity-consumption loop in _increaseHeight completes, lines 1930-1933 execute an additional _crossHeight call when `currentHeight == nextHeightAbove && remainingAtHeight == 0`. This extra crossing is ABSENT from the symmetric _decreaseHeight function. The spurious cross advances `nextHeightAbove` one level further than the consumed liquidity warrants AND writes `feeGrowthOutside` values to the wrong height boundary node. Any subsequent call to getFeeGrowthInside (lines 866-886) subtracts incorrect `lower.feeGrowthOutside` or `upper.feeGrowthOutside` values — producing a corrupted `feeGrowthInside` that may underflow in the unchecked block, yielding an astronomically large fee entitlement (~2^128 tokens).
hypotheses.grounded_in: Confirmed asymmetry between _increaseHeight (post-loop cross present at lines 1930-1933) and _decreaseHeight (post-loop cross absent) from reading FixedHelper.sol. The cross writes feeGrowthOutside to the boundary node via _crossHeight. getFeeGrowthInside consumes those values in an unchecked subtraction block.

hypotheses.exploit_sketch: Attacker (as LP): (1) Provides liquidity at two adjacent heights. (2) Executes a swap that exactly drains lower height (remainder goes to zero), triggering spurious _crossHeight on nextHeightAbove. (3) Calls collectFees — getFeeGrowthInside computes feeGrowthInside using corrupted feeGrowthOutside, underflows in unchecked block, returning (2^256 - dust) / Q128 worth of fees. (4) AMMModule disburses tokens to attacker, draining pool reserves. If balance insufficient, tx reverts but state is permanently corrupted.
hypotheses.victim: Fixed pool LPs and protocol — corrupted fee accounting either overpays one LP (stealing others' fees) or bricks the pool.

hypotheses.title: getFeeGrowthInside unchecked underflow enables massive fee overclaim after height state corruption
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper.getFeeGrowthInside (lines 866-886) computes fee growth inside a range as `feeGrowthGlobal - feeGrowthOutsideLower - feeGrowthOutsideUpper` in an unchecked block. This is intentional for normal wrapping semantics (Uniswap V3 pattern), but relies on the invariant that feeGrowthOutside values are only written via _crossHeight in the correct order. If H-core-pooltype-02's spurious cross writes a large feeGrowthOutside to a boundary not crossed by the position's last update, the subtraction wraps to near-uint256-max. `_collectPositionSide` (lines 474-540) then computes `fee0 = (feeGrowthInside0X128 - feeGrowthInside0LastX128) / Q128` in another unchecked block, yielding a fee entitlement of ~(2^128 - 1) tokens.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read _collectPositionSide at lines 474-540 confirming `fee0 = (feeGrowthInside0X128 - feeGrowthInside0LastX128) / Q128` is in unchecked block. getFeeGrowthInside confirmed unchecked at lines 866-886. Chained vulnerability — depends on H-core-pooltype-02 as trigger.

(5) AMMModule calls FixedPoolType.collectFees → _collectPositionSide → fee0 wraps to ~2^128. (6) AMMModule disburses min(fee0, poolBalance) to attacker, draining pool reserves.

hypotheses.title: SingleProviderPoolType reads stale reserves via VIEW call before hook price query, enabling reserve/price desync
hypotheses.mechanism: SingleProviderPoolType.swapByInput (line 312) and swapByOutput (line 397) read pool reserves via `ILimitBreakAMM(AMM).getPoolState(poolId)` as a VIEW call BEFORE querying the pool hook for the swap price via `getPoolPriceForSwap` (lines 323-326 / 408-412). The reserve value (used to cap output at swapCache.reserveOut) reflects state at the moment of the VIEW call. If the pool hook's getPoolPriceForSwap callback triggers state changes that modify reserves (e.g., via composable hooks that atomically adjust positions), the swap operates on stale reserve data. The AMM's _safeDecrementUint128 at lines 1437/1440 would catch reserve underflow, preventing actual token theft — but the stale read creates a window where the hook can manipulate effective price-reserve combinations not possible with fresh data.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read SingleProviderPoolType.sol lines 312-326 and 397-412. Line 312: `PoolState memory poolState = ILimitBreakAMM(AMM).getPoolState(poolId);` — reserves read before hook price query at lines 323-326.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: Attacker controls pool hook. Hook's getPoolPriceForSwap callback: (1) atomically removes liquidity, reducing actual reserves by X. (2) Returns price computed against original (higher) reserves. (3) SingleProviderPoolType uses stale higher reserveOut as output cap. (4) Attacker extracts X extra tokens in this swap, which AMM's decrement check may catch — but if hook re-adds liquidity after the fact, the circular state confuses accounting.
hypotheses.victim: SingleProvider pool token holders — hook-controlled price combined with stale reserves enables hook operator to extract value.

hypotheses.title: AMMModule._validateProtocolFees DoS on FixedPool swapByInput→swapByOutput fallback path via fee formula mismatch
hypotheses.mechanism: AMMModule._validateProtocolFees (lines 1654-1677) checks `poolProtocolFees >= expectedProtocolFee`. In the partial-fill path (when swapByInput falls back to swapByOutput internally), `expectedProtocolLPFee` is computed using input-path fee formula (`mulDiv` with `poolFeeBPS/MAX_BPS`) but the pool type actually charges output-path fees (`_calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee`: `mulDivRoundingUp` with `poolFeeBPS/(MAX_BPS-poolFeeBPS)`). The output formula yields a strictly higher fee per unit of `reserveAmountIn`. If validation compares pre-fallback `expectedProtocolLPFee` against post-fallback `protocolFee` returned by the pool type and the discrepancy causes `poolProtocolFees < expectedProtocolFee`, the swap reverts — permanently DoS'ing any swap that partially fills a Fixed pool.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read AMMModule lines 1654-1677 confirming expectedProtocolLPFee branch at lines 1666-1672. Read FixedHelper lines 898-931 confirming swapByInput→swapByOutput fallback. Read both fee calculation functions confirming different formulas: input uses `amountIn * bps / MAX_BPS`, output uses `reserveIn * bps / (MAX_BPS - bps)` — the latter is strictly larger per unit.

coupled_pair.reader: AMMModule._validateProtocolFees: checks poolProtocolFees >= expectedProtocolLPFee (computed with lower input rate)

(3) If fee validation reverts, all partial-fill swaps are DoS'd on this pool. Attacker has no profit but griefs users and potentially the protocol's fee revenue.

hypotheses.title: DynamicPoolType.addLiquidity snapSqrtPriceX96 allows unpermissioned price manipulation
hypotheses.mechanism: DynamicPoolType.addLiquidity (lines 232-233) accepts `snapSqrtPriceX96` in user-supplied `poolParams`. If non-zero, it calls `DynamicHelper.snapPrice(ammState, poolId, snapSqrtPriceX96)` BEFORE creating the position. snapPrice moves the current pool price to `snapSqrtPriceX96` — valid only when no active liquidity exists between current and target price. Any caller can pass this parameter since DynamicPoolType has no `onlyAMM` modifier and no authorization check on `snapSqrtPriceX96`. An attacker who provides a tiny liquidity position at the boundary of a range with no active liquidity can snap the price to an extreme, front-running legitimate LPs who expect a stable price.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read DynamicPoolType.sol lines 216-279. Line 232-233 confirmed: `if (liquidityParams.snapSqrtPriceX96 != 0) { DynamicHelper.snapPrice(ammState, poolId, liquidityParams.snapSqrtPriceX96); }`. No authorization check on the snap parameter. DynamicPoolType confirmed to have no onlyAMM modifier.

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper.collectFees compounds four independent Q128 truncations, permanently locking LP fees
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper.collectFees (lines 577-580) calculates fee0 and fee1 by performing four independent integer divisions by Q128: `fee0 = (growthA - lastA) / Q128 + (growthB - lastB) / Q128` and same for fee1. Each division truncates up to Q128-1 units in the X128 domain. With four independent divisions, a position collecting small fees loses up to 4*(Q128-1) X128-units per collection event. A single `(sum_of_growth_deltas) / Q128` would lose at most Q128-1 total, meaning the current implementation loses up to 4x more. These tokens are tracked in AMM feeBalance but are never distributable to any LP.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read FixedHelper.sol lines 577-580. Confirmed four independent Q128 divisions each losing up to Q128-1 X128 units. Pattern: `feeA/Q128 + feeB/Q128` vs optimal `(feeA+feeB)/Q128`.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: Attacker (as LP with many small positions): Repeatedly collectFees across many positions to force maximum truncation. Each collection loses up to 4 wei per token. Over 1M collections: 4M wei locked permanently. Not directly extractable but provably harmful to LP yields.
hypotheses.victim: Fixed pool LPs — cumulative truncation means total claimable fees < total swap fees generated, with remainder permanently locked.

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper._increaseHeight unchecked consumedLiquidity overflow — asymmetric with _decreaseHeight overflow check
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper._increaseHeight (line 1866) uses `unchecked { height.consumedLiquidity += amount; }` with no overflow guard. _decreaseHeight (lines 1763-1767) has an explicit `if (height.consumedLiquidity < amount) revert FixedPool__UnderflowConsumedLiquidity()` underflow check. If consumedLiquidity wraps via overflow, `updateExpectedReserve` computes expected reserves from the wrapped (near-zero) value — making the pool appear to have full reserves when actually depleted. Practically infeasible at current gas costs (~2^256 units to overflow) but represents a meaningful asymmetric safety gap.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read _increaseHeight line 1866 (no overflow guard) and _decreaseHeight lines 1763-1767 (underflow guard present). Asymmetric defensive coding is suspicious.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: Practically infeasible — requires ~2^256 cumulative swaps to trigger overflow. Documents defensive gap only.
hypotheses.victim: Fixed pool LPs — corrupted consumedLiquidity would allow excess reserve withdrawals if ever triggered.

hypotheses.title: SingleProviderPoolType.addLiquidity is external view — full feeBalance returned without state clearance (unlisted fee collection path)
hypotheses.mechanism: SingleProviderPoolType.addLiquidity (lines 180-205) is declared `external view`. If AMMModule._positionAddLiquidity disburses the returned `fees0`/`fees1` to the caller (as a fee distribution concurrent with liquidity addition), an attacker can call addLiquidity with zero amounts to drain the entire feeBalance without providing any liquidity — bypassing the intended collectFees flow.

hypotheses.title: SingleProviderHelper swapByInput→swapByOutput fallback computes fees with different formula, creating directional rounding bias
hypotheses.mechanism: SingleProviderHelper.swapByInput (lines 29-56) has a fallback path: when calculated output exceeds reserveOut, it delegates to swapByOutput with amountOut=reserveOut (line 47). The two paths compute fees differently: swapByInput uses `_calculateInputLPAndProtocolFee` (fee = ceil(amountIn * feeBPS / MAX_BPS)), while the fallback's swapByOutput uses `_calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee` (fee = ceil(reserveAmountIn * feeBPS / (MAX_BPS - feeBPS))). The input path already computed and DISCARDED its fee calculation (lines 33-37); the output fallback recomputes from scratch. The two paths can produce fee values differing by 1-2 wei, creating a systematic directional bias in LP fee collection when the fallback is triggered repeatedly.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read SingleProviderHelper.sol. Lines 42-47 confirmed fallback path. Lines 69-88 confirmed input fee formula. Lines 160-179 confirmed output fee formula. Both use mulDivRoundingUp but with different denominators (MAX_BPS vs MAX_BPS - poolFeeBPS) — the output formula is strictly larger per unit.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: LP exploiting the bias: (1) Find SingleProvider pool near reserve depletion. (2) Systematically trigger fallback swaps (amountIn such that output just exceeds reserveOut). (3) Per fallback, fee difference = 1-2 wei. (4) Over 10,000 fallback swaps: 10,000-20,000 wei of fee drift in LP's favor. Not directly profitable at current gas costs.
hypotheses.victim: Swappers on the fallback path pay marginally higher fees than the input-path formula would charge.

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper._crossHeight fee growth outside flip under rapid height oscillation shifts fee attribution between LP positions
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper._crossHeight (lines 2015-2019) performs the Uniswap V3-style fee growth outside flip: `feeGrowthOutside = feeGrowthGlobal - feeGrowthOutside`. This relies on modular uint256 arithmetic — crossing the same height boundary twice with no fee accrual restores the original value. However, when a height boundary is crossed and uncrossed in rapid succession AND fee growth globals increase BETWEEN the two crosses (from the swap fees themselves), the flip captures the inter-cross fee growth in the feeGrowthOutside value. For positions spanning exactly one side of the oscillated height, `getFeeGrowthInside` will attribute fees differently. An attacker sandwich-oscillating a boundary while holding a position on the benefiting side can extract fees rightfully belonging to other LPs.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read _crossHeight lines 2015-2019 confirming fee growth outside flip. getFeeGrowthInside reads feeGrowthOutside values in unchecked block. Oscillation pattern: cross up (flip), generate fees, cross back down (flip again with new global) — the second flip captures inter-cross fees asymmetrically.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: Attacker with position ABOVE height boundary H200: (1) Tiny zeroForOne swap crosses H200 upward, flipping feeGrowthOutside[H200]. (2) Fees from this swap increase feeGrowthGlobal. (3) Immediately reverse swap (oneForZero), uncrossing H200. Second flip captures inter-cross fee growth in feeGrowthOutside[H200]. (4) Net: fee growth attribution shifts toward ABOVE positions. Attacker's above-boundary position collects more fees than actually earned at the expense of below-boundary LPs.
hypotheses.victim: Fixed pool LPs with positions below the oscillated height boundary — fees they generated are attributed to the attacker's above-boundary position.

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper._collectPositionSide: Unchecked consumedLiquidity Underflow Permanently Corrupts Height Accounting
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper._collectPositionSide (lines 474-539) contains an unchecked block where `height.consumedLiquidity -= (liquidity - sideValue)` is computed. The variable `sideValue` represents the in-range portion of the position at a boundary height; `liquidity` is the position's declared liquidity. If prior partial fills or swapByInput→swapByOutput fallback transitions leave `consumedLiquidity` smaller than `liquidity - sideValue` at collection time, this subtraction silently wraps to near-uint256.max. The corrupted consumedLiquidity is written back to storage and persists forever, causing all subsequent calls to withdrawLiquidity for that height to compute incorrect `value0`/`value1` — either draining excess tokens or bricking withdrawals.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Direct read of FixedHelper.sol lines 474-539. Confirmed unchecked block at ~line 490: `height.consumedLiquidity -= (liquidity - sideValue)` with no underflow guard. Balancer rounding pattern: engineered swap size creates the exact partial-fill state needed to trigger the underflow.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: Attacker: (1) Identifies a FixedPool boundary height where `consumedLiquidity` is near-minimum due to prior partial fills. (2) Calls collectFees or removeLiquidity targeting that boundary. (3) _collectPositionSide underflow wraps consumedLiquidity to ~uint256.max. (4) Other LPs at the same height call withdrawLiquidity — either receive corrupted (huge) amounts draining pool, or tx reverts permanently locking their funds.
hypotheses.victim: Other LPs sharing the same boundary height in the FixedPool — funds stolen or bricked
hypotheses.profit_mechanism: Corrupted consumedLiquidity inflates apparent LP share of the height; attacker withdraws excess reserves beyond deposited amount

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper.withdrawLiquidity: Unchecked withdraw0 = value0 - redeposited0 Underflow — LP Withdrawal Bricked or Drained
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper.withdrawLiquidity (lines 38-124) contains an unchecked block at lines 73-76 computing `withdraw0 = value0 - redeposited0`. The `redeposited0` value comes from `_calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights` (lines 304-390) which calls `addInRange` to adjust amounts for partially consumed heights. When the pool price has moved far into range and many heights are partially consumed, `addInRange` adjustments can produce a `redeposited0` that exceeds `value0`. The unchecked subtraction silently wraps to a huge number. If the AMM transfer then executes, the LP drains tokens far exceeding their deposit; if a downstream reserve check catches it, the LP's `removeLiquidity` call is permanently bricked.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Direct read of FixedHelper.sol lines 38-124 (withdrawLiquidity) and 304-390 (_calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights). Confirmed unchecked lines 73-76 with no guard. ERC-4626 inflation pattern: complex multi-height redeposit logic with two layers of adjustment (consumedLiquidity and addInRange) creates edge cases where redeposited > value.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: LP adds wide range spanning heights 1-100. Sequential swaps consume heights 1-90 (80% of range consumed). LP calls removeLiquidity. _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights computes redeposited0 > value0 due to addInRange over-correction. withdraw0 = value0 - redeposited0 silently wraps. AMM either (a) transfers huge amount to LP draining pool, or (b) reserve check reverts, permanently bricking LP's ability to exit.
hypotheses.victim: LP whose withdrawal is bricked (funds locked); other LPs if huge wrapped amount is transferred (reserves drained)
hypotheses.profit_mechanism: If transfer executes: attacker extracts uint256.max-level tokens minus gas cost; practical impact bounded by pool reserve size

forge test -- contract TestFixedWithdrawUnderflow:
  1. Deploy AMM + FixedPoolType
  2. LP addLiquidity across heights [1, 100] with large amounts
  3. Execute sequential swaps consuming heights 1-90 (80% consumed)
  4. Call FixedPoolType.removeLiquidity (all liquidity)
  5. Assert withdraw0 <= LP's original deposited amount0 (no underflow)
  6. Assert LP receives correct proportion of remaining reserves
  7. chisel fuzz: vary consumed% to find exact threshold where redeposited0 > value0

hypotheses.title: FixedHelper._splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight off-by-one silently recalculates fees with inflated basis (amountIn+1)
hypotheses.mechanism: FixedHelper._splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight (lines 1680-1692) contains: `if (totalAmountInFilled > amountIn + 1) revert`. When `totalAmountInFilled == amountIn + 1` exactly (one wei over due to height rounding), the code does NOT revert but silently recalculates fees using the inflated total as the new basis. LP fee is thus computed on `amountIn + 1` instead of `amountIn`, giving LPs 1 extra wei of fee per occurrence. This edge triggers deterministically whenever cumulative height rounding reaches exactly +1 wei, and an attacker can engineer this via swap size selection.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Read FixedHelper.sol lines 1680-1692. Guard allows `== amountIn + 1` without revert, then recalculates fees with inflated basis. The condition is reachable through specific swap sizes that trigger cumulative height rounding to exactly +1.
hypotheses.exploit_sketch: LP: (1) Binary search for swapAmountIn such that totalAmountInFilled == amountIn + 1 (engineers the rounding edge). (2) Execute that swap — LP earns 1 extra wei of fees. (3) Repeat 1M times: 1M extra wei locked in LP's favor. Not profitable individually but provably triggers systematic fee inflation. Swappers pay marginally more than their swap warrants.
hypotheses.victim: Swappers — each triggered swap pays 1 extra wei of fees to LP. Aggregate: sub-dust but deterministic.
